title: Multilang cluster + relevance harness (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc records a lightweight harness for validating embeddings for multilingual semantic search and clustering. It's intended as a mid-stage onboarding eval for new embedding models and quantized variants, with emphasis on realistic query distribution, cluster sanity checks across languages, and quick human-in-the-loop relevance tests.

Scope:
- Languages: en, es, fr, de, pt, ru, hi, ja, ko (priority ordering)
- Workloads: product search-like short queries (1-6 tokens), conversational queries (3-20 tokens), document-level retrieval (20-400 tokens)
- Targets: evaluate retrieval ranking (nDCG@10, MRR@10), cluster purity/cohesion (ARI, Silhouette), and cross-lingual neighbor consistency (anchor precision)

Dataset composition:
- 5k base docs sampled from internal 'support-docs' + 10 public multilingual wiki pages per language
- Synthetic translations: back-translation pipeline used to create 1:1 mappings for a 600-doc anchor set across 8 languages
- Query pool: 1.2k seed queries derived from logs (anonymized), plus 800 synthetic paraphrases (multilingual paraphrase model)
- Hard negatives: for each query, include 2 model-similar but label-different docs (to stress rankers)

Sampling strategy:
- Stratified by document length and term-frequency buckets
- Ensure at least 50 anchor clusters where cluster members exist in >=4 languages
- For smoke runs, subsample 20% maintaining language balance

Annotation protocol (for human raters):
- Task: given a query and 10 candidate docs, rate relevance on 0/1/2 scale (0:not relevant,1:related,2:direct answer)
- Provide language of query and doc; if rater doesn't know language, they should skip
- Inter-rater: double-annotate 15% of pairs and compute Cohen's kappa; threshold 0.6 to accept batch
- Use provided labeling UI toggles: highlight shared phrases, mark translation-equivalent docs

Metrics and thresholds:
- Retrieval:
  - nDCG@10 (main): baseline target >= 0.62 on en, >= 0.58 on es/fr
  - MRR@10: baseline >= 0.45
- Clustering:
  - Adjusted Rand Index (ARI): baseline >= 0.35 for anchor clusters
  - Average Silhouette: baseline >= 0.18
- Cross-lingual neighbor consistency:
  - Anchor Precision@5: fraction of same-cluster language variants in top-5 neighbors >= 0.72
- Regression rules: any metric drop >3 absolute points from production-verified baseline triggers rollback and forensic run

Smoke-check scripts (dev notes):
- run_smoke_retrieval.sh: runs embedding model against a 1k query shard, outputs ndcg,mrr csv
- cluster_probe.py: computes ARI/silhouette, writes cluster-sample.json for manual inspection
- quick-anchor-check.ipynb: generates a visualization of top-10 neighbors for 50 anchors across languages

Acceptance checklist before model onboarding:
- Unit smoke pass: ndcg/mrr within 1.5 pts of baseline on smoke shard
- Annotation batch: kappa >= 0.6 and no more than 8% skipped due to language issues
- Resource sanity: embedding dimensionality and quantization logged; latency P50 <= 20ms for small queries on test infra
- Sanity review: short write-up (1 page) summarizing failure modes observed and recommended mitigation

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we include low-resource languages (bn, sw) in exploratory buckets? cost vs value?
- Establish automated pipelines to refill hard negative pool periodically (weekly?)
- Decide on drift detection thresholds for cross-lingual neighbor consistency

Owners & timeline:
- Primary: Priya Shah (applied-ml)
- Secondary: Liam O'Connor (platform eng)
- Annotation lead: Chen Wei
- Target: complete first-pass evaluation and report by 2025-02-12 (2-week cycle)

Notes for reviewers:
- This is a working harness; please add comments inline (Google Drive) and link any failing evals as issues to MLINF-842.
- Example quick results attached in linked_artifacts (PR 128 has smoke run csv output)
